reasons: Lake identity gives case_name_full Bennis v. Michigan, court U.S., court_level scotus, date_decided 1996-03-04, year 1996, docket 94-8729.
Lake citations list official 516 U.S. 442, parallel 116 S. Ct. 994 and 134 L. Ed. 2d 68, and vendor-neutral 1996 U.S. LEXIS 1565.

The opinion states petitioner was a joint owner, the car was forfeited as a public nuisance despite her lack of knowledge, and the Court held the order did not offend due process or the Takings Clause.

The opinion separately confirms the due-process rule for innocent owners and rejects the Takings Clause claim because the State lawfully acquired the car through forfeiture rather than eminent domain.
The opinion is centrally about forfeiture of an automobile as a public nuisance and repeatedly frames the issue as whether an innocent owner has a constitutional defense to forfeiture.
The Supreme Court holding on due process and takings consequences of civil forfeiture supports placing the case in Civil Asset Forfeiture with a Key role.
Lens A does not adjudicate treatment or currency defects.
The disclosed lake identity confirms court U.S. and court_level scotus, matching the SCOTUS portion of the authority-weight label.
